h: Torah and Teshuvah Together Heal the Evil Tongue

p: זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת הַמְּצוֹרָע (וַיִּקְרָא יד, ב)
"This shall be the law of the metzora" (Vayikra 14:2).
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (מְצוֹרָע, חֵלֶק ג נג, א)
all the sins of the world
except for that evil tongue, etc.,
דִּכְתִיב זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת הַמְּצוֹרָע כוּ׳
as it is written, 'This shall be the law of the metzora,' etc.:
the law of one who spreads a bad name."
from what they stated as a general rule,
that stands in the way of teshuvah,
the proof he brings cannot be understood,
"This shall be the law of the metzora."
גַּם רַבִּי חַיִּים וִיטַאל זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה
Rabbi Chaim Vital, of holy and righteous memory, also
"Once he has returned in teshuvah, etc.";
for there he made a close reading of
"on the day of his purification, and he shall be brought to the kohen":
the expression "and he shall be brought to the kohen";
after all, the kohen goes out to him
before the Holy One, blessed be He.
since he is sent outside the three camps
and pushed away even from the camp of Yisrael,
has an outcry in his heart:
why has he been pushed out of the community of Yisrael?
But his prayer does not enter, etc.,
for prayer comes from the attribute of Malchus,
is what opens the mouth to pray.
רַבִּי אֱלִימֶלֶךְ זֵכֶר צַדִּיק וְקָדוֹשׁ לִבְרָכָה לְחַיֵּי הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
Rabbi Elimelech, of holy and righteous memory, explained
"From where do we know that the Holy One, blessed be He, prays?":
that is, through the mouths of Yisrael.
And this is what they said (Berachos 34b),
"If my prayer is fluent in my mouth":
until here are his holy words.
And David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
who was a chariot for the attribute of Malchus,
since he has been pushed out of the community of Yisrael,
before the Holy One, blessed be He.
And he said: "Once he has returned in teshuvah
'On the day of his purification, and he shall be brought to the kohen.'"
That is, specifically "on the day of his purification,"
when he purifies himself through teshuvah;
even though he has not yet been purified
by the kohen with the birds,
this is the Holy One, blessed be He,
along the lines of what is written
בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (תַּזְרִיעַ, חֵלֶק ג מט, ב)
and in another place simply 'the Kohen';
and this is the Holy One, blessed be He."
But at any rate it is clear
from the words of Rabbi Yehudah
for spreading a bad name and for lashon hara.
And in truth, something like this
is a dispute in the Gemara (Arachin 15b):
מַה תַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל מְסַפְּרֵי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע
"What is the remedy for those who speak lashon hara?
If he is a talmid chacham,
let him occupy himself with Torah, etc."
"Once he has spoken, he has no remedy,
for David already cut him off with ruach hakodesh,
שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא לִידֵי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע וְכוּלֵּי
That he not come to lashon hara at all, etc."
דּוֹאֵג נִקְרָא אַבִּיר הָרוֹעִים (שְׁמוּאֵל א כא, ח)
Doeg was called "the mightiest of the shepherds" (Shmuel I 21:8),
בֵּין אֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
among those who have no share in the World to Come,
for they are sent out of the category of
by which all of Yisrael have a share.
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי סְבִירָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אַחָא
דְּעַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אֵין תַּקָּנָה
that through words of Torah there is no remedy,
for Doeg declared David forbidden to enter the congregation
and their words of Torah did not help them,
because the yetzer hara blinded their eyes
and to make darkness into light,
so that he declared David's marriage void.
that once one has spoken, he has no remedy through Torah;
That he not come to lashon hara at all.
And the reason the Torah did not help them
to save them from lashon hara
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם וְעַיֵּין סוֹטָה כא, א)
(as they said there, Sanhedrin 106b; and see Sotah 21a).
according to Rabbi Chama b'Rabbi Chanina,
"A healing tongue is a tree of life,"
that breaks the yetzer hara except Torah"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק א רב, א)
and "the light within it brings him back to good"
(as they said in Midrash Eichah Rabbah in the Pesichta, 2,
And Rabbi Acha b'Rabbi Chanina holds
that he has no remedy through Torah,
for David already cut them off with ruach hakodesh,
rather, teshuvah is needed together with the Torah,
that is, through teshuvah he will merit
וְהוּא כְּעֵין מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
This is like what is written in the holy Zohar
for a blemish of the bris;
that stands in the way of teshuvah!
And we said that the meaning is
that teshuvah alone does not help,
for teshuvah comes from Binah, the heart,
while this blemish is in the mind;
and for this, Torah is needed,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר חֵלֶק ב קכא, א)
And this is what it says (Mishlei 4:22),
"and a healing to all his flesh":
and in the opposite way "the flesh of donkeys" (Yechezkel 23:20)
וּכְעֵין מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה יח, א)
And it is like what they said (Rosh Hashanah 18a):
"Through sacrifice and offering it is not atoned,
but it is atoned through Torah."
So too here in the holy Zohar,
that it is not atoned through teshuvah
except when there is Torah with it.
This is exactly like the view of
Rabbi Acha b'Rabbi Chanina in the Gemara,
that the Torah does not help,
and teshuvah is needed along with the Torah.
according to Rabbi Yitzchak in the holy Zohar,
and teshuvah is needed along with it as well;
and according to Rabbi Acha b'Rabbi Chanina in the Gemara,
and along with it he will merit Torah as well.
And this is why Rabbi Yitzchak brought the proof
from the verse, "This shall be the law of the metzora":
"the metzora, on the day of his purification,
the kohen shall go out," etc. (Vayikra 14:3);
הוּא תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע
is the Torah of one who spreads a bad name,
along the lines of what is expounded (end of Menachos, 110a):
זֹאת הַתּוֹרָה לָעוֹלָה וְגוֹ׳ (וַיִּקְרָא ז, לז)
"This is the law of the olah," etc. (Vayikra 7:37):
is as if he offered, etc.;
he needs neither an olah," etc.
That is, Torah is what primarily helps,
that through teshuvah he will merit Torah
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
וְכֵן רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּגְּמָרָא
Likewise Rabbi Chama b'Rabbi Chanina in the Gemara
only he holds that Torah is primary,
and on its account he will also merit teshuvah
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach.
And Rabbi Acha b'Rabbi Chanina in the Gemara
and Rabbi Yitzchak in the holy Zohar
Torah and teshuvah, from the side of the person,
and they disagree as to which is primary:
according to Rabbi Acha b'Rabbi Chanina,
teshuvah, and Torah along with it;
and according to Rabbi Yitzchak in the holy Zohar,
Torah, and teshuvah along with it.
And this is what Rabbi Yehudah said:
"Once he has returned in teshuvah, etc.,
'and he shall be brought to the Kohen'":
that his prayer will be brought,
and he will merit words of Torah as well.
And likewise according to Rabbi Chama b'Rabbi Chanina,
his remedy is to occupy himself with Torah,
and through this he will merit teshuvah,
and his prayer too will be brought
this is the Holy One, blessed be He.
קָרוֹב ה׳ לְכָל קוֹרְאָיו (תְּהִלִּים קמה, יח)
"'Hashem is near to all who call upon Him' (Tehillim 145:18):
'to all who call upon Him in truth.'"
וְכֵן עַל יְדֵי תְּשׁוּבָה גַּם כֵּן
one merits that his prayer be accepted,
which is the attribute of Malchus,
וְגַם תְּפִלָּה בָּא עַל יְדֵי יִרְאָה
and prayer too comes through yirah
(as has been explained in several places from the Gemara).
one merits to enter the camp of Yisrael,
the Torah was given on Shabbos,
And so on Shabbos it is written (Tehillim 92:2),
"It is good to give thanks to Hashem,"
and it says in Pirkei d'Rabbi Eliezer (ch. 19):
"One who confesses and forsakes shall be shown mercy";
כָּךְ הוּא כֹּחָהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה כוּ׳
"Such is the power of teshuvah, etc.;
אָמַר מִזְמוֹר שִׁיר לְיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת כוּ׳
he said, 'A psalm, a song for the day of Shabbos,'" etc.
the spreading of the shelter of peace
for all of them have a remedy.
even for those counted among them
for everyone who is of the seed of Yaakov
will be clarified in the future
